prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create one polished filled-icon concept for the FleaCMS flea mascot, using the attached original outline logo as an identity reference. The user rejected simply filling that exact outline: the large undifferentiated abdomen looked bloated and the thin white stripes looked crude. They explicitly chose: keep the friendly flea, but redraw it as a cleaner filled icon. Preserve recognizable head toward upper left, body to the right, two short antennae, welcoming little smile, small expressive eyes, and springy bent legs. Redraw and rebalance the proportions rather than trace the outline. Head must feel deliberately integrated with the body. Medium: precision flat vector-like logo artwork, confident optical curves and carefully balanced negative space, one ink only, deep navy #142b43 on pure white. No outlines around white-filled body parts. No texture, shadows, highlights, gradients, 3D, typography, framing, props, wings, stinger, furry detail, heart or generic chat-bubble shape. It must read as this friendly flea, not a bee, ladybird, snail, or generic beetle. A single large mark, centered on a square white canvas, taking roughly 76% of canvas width/height with balanced clear margins. No text, no labels, no mockup. Direction D: solve the body as three substantial rounded filled shell sections that nest together, separated by broad, deliberate curved negative-space seams. The silhouette is compact and slightly pear-shaped, with a generous head and shorter abdomen than the reference; do not create a giant empty egg-shaped mass. Each body segment is a filled shape, not a thin band on a solid egg and not a line-drawing stripe. A friendly open white facial area may be used, but it should emerge from the silhouette as an integrated scoop, not a white circle enclosed by a heavy ring. Keep the eye and smile details restrained. Two small bent feet anchor the lower silhouette. Sophisticated friendly software identity. Focus on lovely contour rhythm and the interaction of the three body masses.
approval: Owner selected round 2 concept D on 2026-11-09 and requested deployment everywhere.
